submission:
Root cause: mongodb-rate's pod was created fresh at ~15:01 by platform-automation and then terminated externally by SIGTERM (kill(2) from pid 0/uid 0) within seconds, twice: two clean WiredTiger startup cycles at 15:01:02 and 15:01:04 each ended in signal-handler-driven orderly shutdown, the last at 15:01:10 [tr_9948fd3a2026][tr_fcd9d6881852]. The service itself logged no errors and its storage engine opened, recovered and checkpointed cleanly, so neither corruption, disk, nor storage misconfiguration is the mechanism [tr_fcd9d6881852][tr_4d3c551d555b]. The change set is a first-time workload creation accompanied by a ConfigMap whose name indicates fault-injection/failure-administration intent, landing seconds before the container came up [tr_616998c15f26]. The best-supported reading is an injected/administered kill of the mongodb-rate process: the datastore is absent from the topology while its socket/endpoint churns, leaving callers in the hotel-reservation namespace without a rate datastore. With no metrics available for this service at all [tr_596c016954c3], the mechanism is the process being stopped/killed rather than any value being wrong.
Faulty component: mongodb-rate
Fault type: process_freeze
Confidence: low

Evidence:
- The only log content returned for mongodb-rate in the window is a single burst at 15:01:10 UTC: the process received signal 15 (SIGTERM), reported it as sent by kill(2) from pid 0/uid 0, and then walked through an orderly shutdown sequence (stepping down replication coordinator, closing listening sockets, removing the unix socket file, shutting down storage engine, checkpoint/journal/session-sweeper threads). (found, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The shutdown was externally initiated and clean rather than a crash: the signal handler drove the teardown, replication was marked for clean shutdown, and only 3 in-flight operations were interrupted, indicating low concurrent load at termination time. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The termination occurred at 15:01:10, near the end of the queried window (ends 15:02:30), i.e. well after the start of the window — so it is a late event, not plausibly the trigger of an alert that began earlier in the window. (found, from logql_query on mongodb-rate; query: {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-rate-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})

Reasoning:
Three independent log cuts agree the process was healthy at the storage layer and died to an external signal with no self-reported error, which excludes OOM/segfault (handled SIGTERM path), disk_fill and datastore_corruption (clean recovery, checkpoint, no space or parse errors), and bad_deploy (engine config byte-identical across both starts, first creation rather than a rolling update). The change log places an automation-authored fault-injection-named ConfigMap seconds before the container started, which is evidence for a deliberately induced stop of the process rather than a wrong configuration value doing work in the request path. Remediation is to bring the process back and keep it running (remove the injected kill and restart the workload).

Alternatives considered:
1. mongodb-rate: The PVC rate-pvc was created and updated twice within seconds, and the resulting volume rebind forced the pod to be torn down and rescheduled repeatedly. (bad_config). Ranked lower because: Both engine opens succeeded against a mounted, readable data path with clean journal recovery, so no storage configuration value was actually wrong at the point of failure [tr_fcd9d6881852].
2. mongodb-rate: A lowered memory limit on the newly created workload caused the container runtime to terminate mongodb repeatedly. (resource_exhaustion). Ranked lower because: The teardown follows the handled SIGTERM path with a full ordered shutdown and only 3 in-flight operations interrupted; an OOM kill would be SIGKILL with no such sequence [tr_9948fd3a2026].

Open questions:
- Whether the SIGTERM came from the fault-injection ConfigMap, normal Kubernetes pod lifecycle/rescheduling during first creation, or a liveness-probe failure - no kubelet or pod-event evidence was gathered.
- Whether mongodb-rate stayed down after 15:01:10 or recovered; the log window ends at 15:02:30 and no post-onset startup was observed.
- Which callers (e.g. rate service) actually degraded, and whether they hung to deadline or failed fast - no upstream metrics or logs were dispatched.
- What alert fired at 15:02:21 and on what signal, given Prometheus holds no series for this service [tr_596c016954c3].
